activity_context.topic_title: Symmetry Properties of the Standard Normal Distribution

examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval
examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/f88bf9a66694858e9eaf16f616555eda6d9da7de9f62b678bc1f03b32bf9a620.png)

For a random variable $Z \sim N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a > 0{:}$

$$
P(Z \gt -a) = P(Z \lt a) = \Phi(a)
$$

We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P( Z > -0.76).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/fbacbbe3f53c73316fd070d95e4c077cd695bdcf884d30a95f6b0850df328c80.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z \lt 0.76).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/c0f612336c02eee97d6c66b56f0854286b3a23b90053810e9e4fb75b698b5a60.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z > -0.76)
= P(Z < 0.76)
= \Phi(0.76)
= 0.7764.
$$
